questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I only wanted to go to Paris because i love the city. There is always plenty of htings to do no matter the weather.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing city, made great new friends, lived in a nice place (Cite Universitaire, Swedish House) with great people and genuienly enjoyed every day.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Veery easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had a whole internatonal office with people assigned to differnt parts of the world specifically. Also introduction week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Good introduction week.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy because i just applied to the cite universitarire danish house and got accepted and then send on exchange to the swedish house. You had to make an application though but it was not a lot of work for living in such a nice and calm area with a huge park right next door. The cite also have a lot of sports facilities for very cheap prices.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Apply to the cite! I know that many houses does not have too much 'fællesskab' like there is in the swedish (and danish) house which i have really enjoyed! But even if you want to live on your own the cite is great because then you can just choose to not engage with the others. I would recommend though to get friends where you live but there is also plenty of oppurtunites to get friends through the activities here like the big dining hall you can meet people, petanque courts, volleyball, the sports subspriction, language cafes etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not even consider engaging with the campus-housing possibilites but i have visited friends who lived there and it was clean and nice and they were friends with each other as well.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They created my online account with mails and their 'Absalon' called Moodle which basically works in the same way, so overall very similar to KU in that sense. The exams are offline without any 'hjælpemidler' so there is no exam platform online, they send you a link of where to find your grades which works great.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mails to the international office or just showing up there.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes i wanted but apply for 'forhåndsgodkendelse' for one extra course because two of the ones i wanted was at the same day and time, but i had already gotten 6 approved courses so i could just choose the 5 at the different times. Also i wrote long descriptions for the approval at KU in order to get every course i wanted approved in the first round of applying so i did not have to wait.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is not that many courses in political science to be honest, so if you dont mind not having that large of a selection it is fine. Generally it is easier to go to school at Dauphine but that also depends on your effort. I would advice to take the military strategic planning course because i found that it taught me the most and also had the highest academic expectations which was nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not that large of a selection.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is easier than at KU in the sense that you do not have to read that much, mostly just 1-2 texts per course per week and some courses not anything. You will have to do presentations and you will be evaluated on your in class performance like written work and oral participation kind of like in high school. The exams were almost all essays in 3 hours which i also find way easier than back home. You do have to remember all of the syllabus in your head though but it was not that difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very high school like here in France, but generally a very high level of participation from the students. I really liked how many of the professors encouraged discussions and sharing our perspectives especially as we came from all over the world.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
'Secrets to conflict resolution and cooperation'
'Mass media in the digital age: can it survive?'
'Global climate politics'
'Introduction to military planning'
'Understanding contemporary issues: A sociological outlook'

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
'Introduction to military planning' was very insightfull, hard power, highly skilled and intelligent professor, high expectations, really learned a lot from this course.
'Global climate politics' if you like the COP UN this is for you, touches on US throughout history and Chinas influence today on COP and the climate agenda in general
'Understanding contemporary issues: A sociological outlook' very knowledgeable professor who were good at making up examples and getting everyone to participate.
'Secrets to conflict resolution and cooperation' very fun weekendcourse where you learn how to handle conflicts but not very politcal at all (can be used in a political setting though) but not theoretical in the sense we know from back home.
'Mass media in the digital age: can it survive?' basically just the professor yapping for 3 hours each week but if you want to chill more and relax this is for you.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Ehm my shopping went a little crazy. Too many good vintage stores.
Paris is not really that expensive compared to Copenhagen like i would say you could definetly survive with a 4000DKK budget per month for food, phone, sports, transport etc. but it is more fun to have more. I have spend a lot of my own money as well but that is only because i shopped so much, traveled around and when you have visitors from home go out to eat all the time.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Nothing really, i just spend a lot of money shopping and getting great food and coffee.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not participate in the Dauphine sports program but i know they have a lot of it for very good prices.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every type of sport, i think language cafes, parties. I mostly participated in all that was going on in the Cite where i lived.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sports! Very fun, cheap, meeting new people.
Asking people to go out for dinner happened a lot which was so fun, everyone is here on limited time and has no friends either and want to see Paris.
Walking around lol, you always stumble upon something too see, eat or drink.
Museums! so many good ones for free if you are under 25 and from the EU.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Walk around the city, Paris is endless and there is a million guides on the internet of what to do and see in Paris so just search!
My favorite things to do are sit in the Luxembourg garden, go to the Musee Rodin, go up the Pantheon for free to see the views of Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy but i have also been to Paris many times and feel at home. The biggest challenge is the language but i spoke A2 level french before coming here which have been very sufficient in the day to day life, sometimes i wish i could speak more because of the people in my house are almost everyone fluent in french but i have evolved a lot thorugh practice. I would advice practicing french because even to´hough many frenchmen are nice and let you speak broken french or english they very much prefer having conversations in french and do view you as a bit rude if you do not speak a word.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get a tutor/mentor at dauphine, they sent an email and you say yes. Boom already one french friend. Go to the parties. Speak french or it will be difficult.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language. It is very frustrating sometimes not being able to express yourself or understand what is being said - and some french people cant or refuse to speak english.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture of sitting in cafes and parks with your friends, eating and drinking late into the night even on weekdays. Parisians really enjoy hanging out in the city which i do too.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The university building is not as nice as KU back home but whatever.
The classes are easier so you will have to motivate and set goals for yourself.
It is easy to get help.
I really liked going to Dauphine.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Throwing myself into situations i had never tried before, meeting new people, starting from scratch in a new country having to build you own life, living in a 'kollegie' speaking a foreign language constantly, spending time alone, just showing up to things not knowing anyone there.
Really make it a challenge for yourself and get out of your comfortzone has taught me so much

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go on exchange, it has been the best experience and i have learned so much about myself. Basically lived my dream life.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
